utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Mr. Registrar. Let me greet the Prosecution bench. Good afternoon, Mr. Witness. You appeared before us several weeks ago. My greetings to the Defence counsel, to the accused. There is still one who is not totally recovered. I hope he will be with us very soon. Let me give the floor to Mr. Registrar for some IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: OTP has submitted a lot of documents to be tendered through Ferida Likic; the list shall be given IC number 508. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. The -- we're going to he resume with the witness's cross-examination. With regard to time allotted, at the time we had given 45 minutes for each of the Defence teams for cross-examination purposes, all together 240 minutes. As to that -- as to the time used until now, 118 minutes, 47, for 5D, 32 minutes for 1D, 21 for 2D, and 18 minutes for the 3D team. Mr. Praljak, in other words. So you still have 122 minutes. Let me remind you if you refer to incidents 8 and 14 of the report you'll have to ask to move into private session since you would be dealing then with protected witnesses. This is all I had to say. I believe that it is now Mr. Praljak who must continue with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. May I kindly ask you at the very beginning since I'm going to deal with the technical aspect of your expertise, trajectories, angles, speed, velocity of the bullet, entry and exit wounds, I would appreciate it if your answers to it my technical questions could be as short as possible. If the question is clearly phrased, I would like your answer to be brief because I am under certain time limitations, and we do have to cover quite a number of incidents. Thank you very much in advance. May I now kindly ask for 3D 00849. 3D 00849. In your earlier testimony you said that you did not properly inspect the house on Stotina from which there was a sniper shooting, in your opinion because there were mines around, and I am therefore producing a record on the removal of mines from the area around the building and inside the building. It's 3D 00849. My question is, did you know that that area was de-mined, according to all regulations, that it was handed over, taken over as de-mined and that the de-mining enterprise was paid for by the government of the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We still can't see the document -- oh, yes, it is here. I won't go on about this. This document shows everything that is necessary to prove that that area de-mined. The date is 9 September, 2004. But let us move on. You did not inquire in the proper place whether the -- this location was de-mined or not, cleared for mines?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We inquired at the -- the field office in Sarajevo as to whether the area -- there were dangerous areas still in the vicinity of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to move to another incident, documents 3D 00768. Again, 3D 00768. Give me just a second. Incident number 9. It involves a boy of around 14 who was hit in Orucevica street, Donja Mahala neighbourhood. You have drawn a sketch here and I would like quickly to go through the technical aspects of this. You say that the distance from Stotina was 470 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the distance that I measured with the laser range finder, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please, let us note the initial velocity of the bullet. Do you agree that calibre 7.62 times 51 millimetre has the initial velocity of 860 metres per second?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends on the rifle, but it would be just around the right velocity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that calibre 70 -- sorry, 7.9 times 57 millimetres in an M-76 sniper rifle has the initial velocity of the bullet of 730 metres per second?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to know that out of my head right now at this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I read the information from the technical specification attached, and that is verifiable. My next question: The last time I showed you a table, an Eberhard and Hinbert [phoen] table where the median velocity where running of a 14-year-old boy is 4 metres per second or thereabouts. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that would be a fair conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we further agree that the time the bullet takes from leaving the barrel, and according to the speeds I've read, crosses the distance of 470 metres in .6 to .7 [Realtime transcript read in error,"2.7"] seconds?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be about the right time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have a problem with the record, line 15, page 4. The question was from .6 to .7 seconds, whereas the record says .6 to 2.7. That needs to be corrected now. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you please answer, if the boy appears on the corner and crosses 2 metres in .5 seconds until the spot where he was hit, so he crosses 2 metres in half a second, and the bullet takes .6 or .7 seconds until that same spot from the moment that it was ejected from the barrel, how can these two bodies meet at the same spot at two different times? We have a technical problem there. And the problem is the boy, of .6 or .7 seconds would not be in that spot even if we set aside the time necessary to locate a target, to aim at a target, and pull the trigger.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is indeed difficult to hit a target moving at that speed at that distance, but it's -- with anticipation it is still possible. And if I make a comparison to a shooting range where you have pop-up targets that are operated radiographically or manually, they will get up, but if -- if you've been on the shooter range for a longer time you would still be able to -- you know the exact location where the target will appear, and if you shoot the target it falls away, it will swing up again. If you start shooting when the target is still down, the bullet will be there when the target is coming up and hitting the target again. So it is possible with anticipation, but it is difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, what does anticipation mean unless it is blind shooting? According to my technical data, it means that somebody fired before having seen the target. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way it is. Anticipation in this incident would be that the shooter who might have been at the -- shooting location for a longer time would have known -- would have seen people moving the same -- along the same path time and time again, so he will know when someone looks around the corner to see if it's clear and will then move. He will know that -- his target will move in that direction. So it's not a -- it's still a very lucky shot to hit the target, but it's -- it's possible, and that's what I mean with anticipation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, sir. We're talking about technical data here. The bullet left the barrel and on the assumption that he had seen the boy, that the shooters had seen the boy, the bullet would have reached that spot in .1 to .2 seconds?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me, how much time does a sniper need to locate a target, to aim at it, and pull the trigger? How much time does that require for a moving target?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately one second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 1 second and 6/10ths. So aiming at a non-existing target, the shooter fired and the bullet and the boy met after the boy started running.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to pull the next picture that deals with the same problem. The same number, just the next sheet, please. Please have a look. No, no, no. The next page, please. We've seen this page. Next page, please. No, I mean my drawing, my drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: There was a misunderstanding. The previous one, which was on ... THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While this is being put on the screen, do you remember that the boy sustained an entry and exit wound in the left side of his stomach, the exit side being on the back, again on the left side of the boy's body, but it was absolutely parallel. The entry and exit wound was absolutely parallel to the ground level, and the boy was hit on the left side of his stomach, and the exit wound is on the right side of his back in the abdominal area. Can we turn the page that shows this. The same exhibit number, next page. I will use up too much time this way. While this is -- no, no, not this one. Can we please put this sheet on the ELMO. Look at this photograph, the photograph clearly shows that it's the left side of the stomach, and the -- there is a wound on the right side of the boy's back. In fact, he is a young man now who appeared in this courtroom earlier. Do you agree that the entry wound is on the left side of the stomach and the exit wound is on the left side of his back?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we now see the drawing that I produced, the next page. Could you please put it on the ELMO. No, no, the next one. Just turn that page. No. Please take the sheet that I'm holding. We have seen it before. I don't understand how it can't be produced again. Please, Witness, look. Does this correctly depict the movement of the boy from that corner forward? Is that correctly drawn?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be an assumption because he was moving from one corner to the other, but he had to move around the fence that is in my drawing. So he would be moving around it. So it wouldn't be a straight path but just -- but -- it would be the direction that he was moving, yes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it was not to -- completely straight line, but the direction is shown directly, isn't it? It was at a right angle to the trajectory of the bullet, if the bullet was coming from Stotina. Could we agree that the bullet was coming from the right side as juxtaposed to the movement of the boy?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible, and if it is possible, how, if the movement of the boy was at a right angle to the trajectory of the bullet for the wound to be on the left side of the stomach? According to the laws of physics and geometry, is that possible?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the boy was moving exactly without turning to that, then it would be impossible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course we can speculate that the boy may be stopped or turned, but the boy was running, knowing that it was dangerous ground. He had four metres to cover, and he did run those four metres. That's what he testified. If that is correct, then it would be impossible for a bullet coming from his right to inflict a wound on the left side of his stomach. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we now see 3D 00847. In particular, photograph 3D 23-0245. 3D 23-0245. Witness, do you see on this photograph this boy, who is now a young man, showing the exact spot of his exit wound? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the left side of his back?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In conclusion, can we agree that it is much more likely, in fact it is the only likely possibility from all we know, that the bullet came from the opposite direction and that only a bullet coming from the opposite direction could have hit the boy, moving as he was, in the left side of his stomach and exited on the same side through the back?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not of that opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not of the opinion that the boy was running towards the bullet?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If the direction that the bullet originated from was exactly the opposite side, it would be at the wall -- the shooter would have to be against the wall three metres away from the victim, which seems to me very unlikely. If you -- if you look at the -- my sketch, the layout of the -- of the incident site --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your sketch we clearly see that the street towards which he wanted to run is a very open space and that at the moment he was hit he had already cleared the wall. You don't agree with my proposition, or maybe you agree that the bullet could have come only from the direction in which the boy was moving, straight forward into that street. Yes or no? We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Thank you very much. Can we now move on to incident number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there is no answer recorded in the transcript. I don't know whether there was any, but it should be recorded in that case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My answer was no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That was not recorded. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we please have 3D 00765.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is incident number 2, which is at Gojka Vukovica Street. A water tank truck was hit. Please have a look. At Gojka Vukovica Street in front of two buildings, you drew the water tank truck as having been parked in front of the second building, looking toward the north, and that the bullet arrived from Stotina. Is that correct? Is this consistent with your sketch?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You calculated the coordinates at which this took place. My question is as follows: According to you, the corner of the right-hand building, the -- the building in its height, did it obstruct the view towards Stotina? You did not take that corner of the street -- corner of the building into account, but when you were visiting the site were you able to see the place where the water tank truck was parked from Stotina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the witness testifying about this event drew the water tank truck as having been marked more to the south, in front of the first building, in fact?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building that you mean -- described in your sketch with A? Is that the first building?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You drew the water tank truck in front of that building, whereas the boy drew the water tank truck as having been parked in front of the building I marked as B. Are you aware of the fact that you and the witness had quite the opposite opinions as to where the water tank truck was at the time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I -- the information that I had and the exact spot that was pointed out to me by the investigator on the scene was the location that I drew in my sketch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could we please turn to the second sheet of the same document, my sketch. Here. Have a look. The place where the boy marked the water tank as having been parked is drawn in red, and we see your sketch of the water tank as well. The difference in altitude between the water tank truck cab and the point Z at Stotina, are you aware of it? Do you know what the difference in altitude is between the water tank and the house at Stotina from which, to your knowledge, the water tank was fired at? Do you know the difference? Did you calculate it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only calculated the elevation from my location, of the location that I had for the water truck. So I didn't have the difference in altitude for the location where the boy said his -- the water truck was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please give me specific answers. My question is quite specific. Do you know the difference in altitude from -- between the place where the water tank was and Stotina? Do you or do you not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please pull up document 3D 00756 on our screens. 3D 00756. I will show you a host of photographs I asked to be taken at the time when we were having a recess in the proceedings. This photograph was taken from the point where the boy said the water tank truck was parked, in front of the first building, facing Stotina. Can you see -- can one observe Stotina from this spot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see Stotina on this photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that if we move the water tank truck back, the building will obstruct the view of Stotina, which cannot be seen as it is anyway, even more? Therefore, if we move to the spot where you said where the water tank was, will we not obstruct the possible view of Stotina even more?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It will be -- if the truck would be moving away, the angle would be towards -- Stotina will be smaller, and therefore it would be more likely for the target to be visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer was entered in the transcript, although it goes against the elementary rules of geometry. Let's have 3D 2205 -- or, rather, 0657. That's the next photograph. This photograph was taken from Stotina, from the forward left part of it. Do you see the two buildings up front? No, this is 743. I would like us to show 3D 22-0765, although we can stay with this one. 743, yes. Look at this photograph. Do you see the two buildings in front of which the water tank was parked as we see them? Can you in any way see a water tank parked in front of the two buildings to our right as you are looking at the spot now?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect, I don't see the area where the truck is supposed to be. It's too -- is not enough detail to distinguish the buildings for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have cypress trees there, but I see you can't tell. Well, can we have document 3D 00845. It will make the exercise somewhat easier. 3D 00845. On that photograph you will see the building at Stotina -- or, rather, the house that was constantly referred to as the place where the sniper shooter was located. You see, I went my investigators out afield, and I asked them to climb the ladder up to the window that could best be used as the shooting position. Do you recognise the building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have this document bearing the same number and photograph number 0235. 0235. From the position where the gentleman standing on the ladder was, the camera faced the opposite side, i.e., the place where the water tank was located. Can you recognise on this photograph behind the Cyprus trees those two white buildings in front of which in are view water tank that was hit was located?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just -- just one question, because you said just two minutes ago that the photos were taken -- the first photo you shown was from the left side of the building and this is from the right side of the building. So this is -- these photos are taken from the right window on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This position is much more appropriate to achieve the hit, because the more we move to the right the more the view is obstructed. And as we move to the left we see the back side of the buildings. So I tried to move to the right-hand side to see whether from the further-most right-hand side window one could see the location or not. Let's look at the photograph again. Do you recognise the buildings?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the cypress trees and the buildings behind it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic tells me that the transcript contains an error. The more we move to the left-hand side within the building at Stotina the less likely are we to see the buildings on the right. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we look at photograph 236 now. My investigators took the necessary steps, which was they took a tele-photo lens and tried to take photographs zooming in the spot where the water tank should have been. Do you recognise now behind the cypress trees the two buildings we've been referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have photograph 238. 238. This is the photograph taken with the use of the objective lens, and is it clear to you now, sir, that if the water tank had been located in front of that building that was further away it was quite unlikely for that spot to have been observable from the Stotina building?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Praljak please repeat the last part of his question. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The water tank at the location where you placed it, would you have seen it from this spot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the location that I took the photograph, which was also on the right-hand side in front of the window in a direct line from the window to the incident site, which produced the photo that I provided in the report, which shows for me that the target would have -- of the water truck would have been visible in front of the second building. So from your pictures I would say it would be very difficult to see the target from that location, but from my pictures that I took, it would be very visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please take a look at your photograph at page 12 of the Croatian version. Look at your photograph, and please explain to me what your photograph shows. It doesn't show either of the two buildings, nor does anyone know what the photograph shows, which section of the street. Your photograph does not show either of the two buildings, and it is quite unclear as to what in fact you took the photograph of. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what did you take the photograph of? Which section of the street? If we can't see the section in front of the buildings where the water tank was located, what do we in fact see here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you -- as you've shown me -- shown to me a while ago the cypress you see in the -- on the left corner of my photograph, it's the same cypress that's visible on the right side of photo 0238, but my photo shows more of the street, and it tries to show the exact incident site. So the trees you see that fill the left side of the street are the trees in front of the two buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could we please be shown the picture the witness has taken, because we do not have it on the screen. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] In the witness's material, that's at page 12 of his report, in the Croatian version, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record - sorry, Your Honour - it's P 09808. P 09808 in the report. It's page 12 on the hard copy or page 13 in e-court. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here is the photograph you took, sir. On this photograph, we can't see the buildings in front of which, according to your knowledge or the witness's knowledge, the water tank was located. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How are we able to know what it is you wanted to show on this photograph unless you also include in the photograph the place where the water tank was parked? You obviously took the photograph of the front part of the street where the water tank was not parked; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the photograph of the location from -- in front of the house of Stotina toward the location where I -- where my information said the water truck was located, which is shown by the arrow, case number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell me where is the building on the left-hand side which you drew in the earlier sketch? Where is it? In the earlier sketch you drew the water tank in front of one building and there is another one next to it, and here, quite arbitrarily, you showed the spot where some other water tank was located but certainly not the one from the earlier sketch; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. The buildings start to -- to appear in the left-hand side just beyond the -- the cypress and more to the left. So the buildings are not visible. What is visible is the garden that is visible on -- that I've drawn into my sketch, which is marked by the trees in the photograph. The reason why the buildings are not visible is because I took the photo through a pair of binoculars, laser range finders, which narrowed the field of view but give a very detailed picture of the exact incident site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we disagree fully, because the buildings cannot be seen on this photograph. They are to the far left. You can agree with me or not, but I will tell you that the place that you drew on the sketch as the place where the water tank was is certainly not depicted in this photograph. Now, would you agree or disagree with me?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have 3D 00771. 3D 00771. This refers to two incidents, namely incident number 8 and 14. These two incidents -- yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You only deal with technical details. There's no need for a private session otherwise. Yes, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I was just making the same point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. So, Mr. Praljak, please continue. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will be dealing with technical matters from the expertise alone. I simply want to show the way in which the expertise was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These two events or incidents took at Brace Brkica Street, could we please see 3D 00771.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but this document hasn't been released in e-court. If it could be released, then ... THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Give me a moment, please. 3D -- very well. Let's look at page 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my information, 3D 771 is something that should be in e-court, but you can place it on the ELMO. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] No, no. This is not it. This is not it. I will give you my copy, please. Perhaps I made a mistake. Who knows. Perhaps we can deal with 3D 771 later. I made a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there were two incidents that took place there at the sidewalk next to the intersection between Marsala Tita and Brace Brkica Streets; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with the way the incidents were marked, because one took place in the vicinity of the other.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we please have 3D 00844 shown. And then photograph 3D 23-0206. 0206. 3D 00844, photograph 0206. Do you know that what we see in the foreground is Brace Brkica Street, and the street running parallel to the brown building is Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please have the next photograph, 207. 207. Is this the spot where the two incidents took place on the sidewalk right here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it didn't look exactly same location, but it was in the vicinity of this location, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what vicinity -- what was the vicinity of the two incidents? Can you draw and mark on this map where the two incidents took place? If you're not able to, we can move on. We've already dealt with this. We don't have to go back to it. If you know, fine. If you don't, fine again.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need a different photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please have photograph 209 -- or, rather, sorry, 208, 208. To your knowledge, was this photograph taken exactly from the spot where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be the exact location of incident 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now have photograph 211. From this same spot a number of photographs were taken with an objective lens toward the direction where the two men were hit at different times. Is that the same photograph depicting the scene of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have photograph 212, and could 213 be prepared. 212. Sir, can you see Hotel Bristol here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see -- we've already discussed under whose control Hotel Bristol was, but do you see a single spot from which -- I mean, any spot under the control of the Croatian Defence Council, from which it was possible to shoot at a spot where two persons were hit? Do you see a single building controlled by the HVO at the time of the conflict in Mostar that provides the possibility for shooting at the spot where two persons were hit? Yes or no? Or maybe you don't know.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Photograph 213, even closer up. 213. Have a look. Do you know that all the buildings we see here were under the control of the BH army at the time of the conflicts in Mostar? If you don't know, that's good enough.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we now please have photograph 214. It's a whole series of photographs that I had made from the Spanish Square and possible shooting from the Spanish Square from the crowns of trees or maybe from a platform or a ladder, or a platform provided by a truck. Do you recognise this spot? We see a high school there and the Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the Spanish Square, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the left side of that photograph is an area held by the BH army at the time of the conflicts? You see those devastated buildings, that side.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the next photograph would be 215. They were taken anti-clockwise. The next one is 215. So we are moving towards the location of the incident, the possible incident, and this is a street leading towards Marsal Tito bridge. Do you recognise it? Do you know it was under BH army control?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 216, please. Do you recognise this area? It's the street leading towards Marsal Tito bridge and further on to the area where the incidents took place. Is it possible to see the location of the incident in any way from here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that exact location, no, it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To speed up things a little we'll skip a number of photographs, but they can stay on file. Let's move on to 221. This photograph faces west. It's taken from the same spot as the ones before. The area controlled by the HVO. Do you recognise that it is the Spanish Square and that the camera is facing west?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Photograph 221, please, now -- sorry, 222. This photograph will again show part of the high school, the camera facing west, and we see a long alley of trees in Mostar from a place where you concluded there could have been a platform providing a good view for shooting. Do you recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the area, but this is not the area that I indicated as the origin of fire. The area that I indicated was in 3D 23-0220 and 0221.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Photograph 223, please. And could 224 be on stand-by, please. On photograph 223, since you mentioned in your testimony the crowns of trees where the shooter could have been, I placed my man on top of a ladder. Do you see the man on the ladder?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph, please. It was taken from the spot where the man atop a ladder was. Photograph 224, facing east. Does the photograph show abundantly clearly that this spot where the plain trees were does not provide a view of the site of the incidents at all?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this location doesn't provide a -- a view of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Photograph 225, please, which is only closer up, the same thing. Is it even more clear here that from that spot it was impossible to shoot towards the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Photograph 227, please. 227. I placed my man next on a very tall ladder, and the location is now such that the Spanish Square is on the right. Do you see the man on the ladder?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that spot a number of photographs were taken. 228, please, then 229. A whole series of photographs, and they all face the incident site. The purpose was to see if the incident site was visible even from a platform, from an elevated position, even if we set aside the fact that the war was going on at the time and there was the front line between the two warring factions in the middle. Is it possible to shoot at Brace Brkica Street from here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this location it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph, please, closer up, 230. Do you see that it's simply impossible to see the incident site because the street is a meandering one?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the location that this photo was taken it is impossible to see the location of the incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Photograph 232, please. The cameraman had the task to establish whether it was possible to see the incident site from any spot at all, the Spanish Square or anywhere else, so he kept moving further to the right. Do you see the man?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the man on the ladder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last photograph, 233. Do you see that even from this location we do not have a view of the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we had certain witness statements, can you agree with what I'm going to say now: There was not a single location under HVO control that made it possible to shoot at the incident site in Brace Brkica Street, 1814 [as interpreted]? Not a single spot provided a view of the man at incident site number 8 or number 14?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that the sniper would be in any spot located in a site under HVO control? Why don't you agree? Where in that case, according to you, was the sniper located?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've mentioned in the report, the photo that I took of the incident site where the -- the red building, or the red-brown building, is clearly visible with the markings 1904, that building is clearly visible in my picture, and I haven't seen it -- I've only seen the top half visible in some of the pictures provide by you. I took the photograph from the platform in the direction of Brace Brkica Street towards the incident site, and in my photograph it is possible to get a view of the incident sites, especially if you're go on a slightly higher level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at your photo on page 26 of the Croatian version of your report. Look at it. I'm not saying from where you can see a certain building. I'm asking you to show me the exact spot in which in your opinion the sniper shooter was looking at the man located in the way we have heard they were located in incident number 8 or 14. Look at your own photograph. In my personal view, it shows absolutely nothing. It's on page 26 of the report, the Croatian version. It's not the one, but again that's the photograph you took. Next photograph. Raise it a bit. Further up, please. Now, tell me, what do we see on this photograph? Do we see the spot where two men were hit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said before, it's -- it shows all the surroundings of the exact incident site, but I wasn't able -- at that time I wasn't able to go to a more elevated position. My photo was taken from above approximately two metres of height. If I would be at a position two metres higher, I would get a clear view of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you, sir, what you were able to do. I'm asking you if we can see on this photograph the spot where people were hit. Can you tell me from which exact location you photographed this? I put it to you that you were not able to photograph this from Spanish Square, number one; and number two, I put it to you that this photograph does not show the spot where the people were hit.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph is taken from exactly the same position that is shown in the picture of page 39 of my copy, the other photo that's included, some two pages. It's with both cases. That is 20 -- 25 and 39. It's the same picture. That is the exact location from where I took the picture towards the incidents sites. The man behind the -- the laser range finder is the investigator on scene. And the concrete structure you see behind this, the one that's also visible in the pictures you provided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, the building on the left, the left building that we see, and the Judges will make the comparison, does not depict the left building on the corner of Marsala Tita and Brace Brkica Street. This secessionistic style of architecture or whatever it is doesn't have anything to do with the corner of Brace Brkica Street that is relevant. Do you claim that what you photographed is the corner of Marsala Tita street and Brace Brkica Street? Is that the corner?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location where the arrow is pointing, that's an exact location. The old building on the left-hand side it's the same building as the old building in 3D 23-0211, the old building with the shed in front and the roof of the -- angled roof of the shed is also visible in my picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will leave it to the Trial Chamber to analyse and compare, but my assertion is that the building we see on the left here is not the building on that corner. I have one more matter for you. Can you please place this on the ELMO. Meanwhile, can we have 3D 00771 ready, and we'll deal with this one very briefly. With incident number 2, you calculated east as 17 degrees, 49 minutes, and 9.-something seconds, whereas incident 3 is 17 degrees, 98 minutes and .2 seconds. I did some reckoning myself. Do you agree that 1 minute has 60 seconds in sphere geometry, and 1 degree is 60 minutes?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the equator is about 40.000 kilometres long, which means a half of the equator is 20.000 kilometres? And when we divide it into 180 degrees, which is the amount we have from Greenwich towards the east, it turns out that 1 degree is approximately 100 kilometres. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if 100 kilometres are divided into 60 minutes, then it's -- then 1 minute is approximately 1.7 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it then correct that if an incident has 49 minutes and another 98 minutes - could we scroll down a bit? - that the difference is around 15 minutes, and 15 minutes multiplied by 1.7 kilometres is around 75 -- 85 kilometres, the difference between two incident sites? Is my arithmetics correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you, how could you have made such a major error if the incidents were 85 kilometres away from one another? How can an expert make such a major error in view of the distance from Greenwich?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a writing error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the GPS system you used, do you know what the standard margin of error it has in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, very sorry. We haven't received the answer from the witness previously, so be so kind to repeat it again to the -- I mean, your answer to the previous question. Actually, it is by Mr. Praljak. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand. It was probably a writing error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Your Honour, page 26, line 23, you still have it on your screens, it says the distance -- the difference is 15 minutes, whereas in fact Mr. Praljak's question referred to 5-0, 50 minutes' difference. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question, Witness, is this: Before measuring by GPS, did you know what is the standard margin of error for your device?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The standard margin of error for my personal GPS is five metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You think. Do you know or do you think?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long ahead of your measuring did you check the GPS device when you calibrated it or standardised it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the GPS -- the GPS coordinates were provided me by the Prosecutors. I didn't always use my GPS to measure the exact location. Some were -- some were -- I took as GPS and some were pointed out to me by the investigator on scene, according to the DVD.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 3D 00 -- THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to have a break. The time has come for a break. It's 20 to 4.00. We will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. We can start again. As far as time is concern, I was told that there's -- Defence still has 42 minutes, but I've understood that 4D needed 10 minutes, and 6D, I don't know. So, Mr. Praljak, you know exactly what you need to know now. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry that we're unable to go through all these incidents properly, but I will go as far as I can. Can we look at incident 1, 3D 00771?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we have a man who was hit from the distance of 760 metres in his leg according to this sketch. Sir, do you see the sketch?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The spot where the man was hit in his leg in relation to the direction of the bullet was at the alpha angle, which is roughly 45 degrees, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to conclude that from my information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page, please. We will see the photograph where the witness told us -- and this is the photograph from the same bundle. Look at the anatomy of a person from the back, as the witness shows us how he was hit while he was standing next to the wall. He was hit in the back above the knee. That was where the entry wound was. And the exit wound was at the parallel -- or, rather, was at the parallel height, and it exited just above the knee. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's the information supplied by the witness, I suppose it's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although you didn't answer my question. My question was did you have any documentation as to the entry wound and exit wound?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only documentation to me was the information on the DVD where the victim shows his -- the location of his wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we turn to the next sheet. At what angle would the entry/exit wound have been if we assume that the shot was fired from Stotina? Do you know what the difference in altitude is between the spot where the sniper shooter might have been active and the spot where the victim was? What -- or where the person hit was. What's the difference in altitude?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now look at some photographs from 3D 00846. Photograph 240. Are you familiar with this reconstruction put forth by the person who was hit? He said, "I stood thus, leaning against the wall when the bullet hit me above the knee of my right leg." Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are stills from the DVD. I recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How can you explain then that the entry/exit wound does not correspond with the angle which should have been shot at had the shooter been in fact at Stotina? How do you account for the fact that the entry/exit wound is parallel, whereas Stotina is on much higher ground? Can you answer briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question: If the position of this man, which is quite clear from the sketch, is that he faced the Neretva with his back and Stotina stands at exactly 45 degrees' angle in relation to his position, how could he have been shot from the back then and not at a 45-degree angle, which would mean more to the side? How can you account for the bullet trajectory and the positioning of the entry and exit wounds?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came to the conclusion that Stotina was the most likely origin of fire not only based on -- not -- solely based on the images from the DVD, and for him the incident was also a long time ago, so I don't know if it's exactly precisely the same position he was in. But looking at this still from the DVD, if he had been positioned like this and the -- the bullet of the entry and exit wound would have been of -- since they were completely parallel, they shooter would have to be in the river, because he's pointing with his thigh slightly upwards. So then -- yeah. So it's very difficult to get an exact location from the shooter from only his entry and exit wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the basis of the position of the body, would you agree with me the bullet could have reached him from his back, which means from possibly the river or the hillside beyond it? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction physically where the bullet might have originated from could include that direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we please have 3D 00769. 3D 00769. That's incident number 10, yet again involving Stotina. 3D 00769. You drew the possible line of movement according to the witness's testimony in the direction of the stair -- of the stairs. Is your sketch accurate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Stotina is located at an angle higher than 45 degrees in relation to the direction in which the person who was hit was moving. Is that correct based on your sketch of the bullet trajectory?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the elevation you talk about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. It's on the right side. If the aggrieved person is moving from the Neretva, as you drew it, the direction in which Stotina lies, again according to your sketch, is at some 45 degrees. That's what I'm asking you. In relation to the person moving.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We have seen this, and I will show it to you on the photograph, that the bullet hit him in the heel in the general area of where the Achilles tendon is, and it exited just where the heel is. So it -- the bullet entered the body at roughly 45 degrees compared to the axis of the leg. It entered roughly the area where the Achilles tendon is - you can see it on my sketch - at a 45-degree angle compared to the axis of the human body. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the bullet entered the Achilles tendon and exited at the heel parallelly, then it did not arrive from either the right or left side. Can we conclude that the position in which the person was -- can we show photograph 3D 00848, photograph number 251. 3D 00848, photograph 21 -- 251. Do you agree that the person showed exactly the position in which his body was when he was hit or right before he was hit? Do you see that? Is that visible?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he turned with his back to the Neretva River?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is his side turned towards Stotina, that we might possibly see in the background laterally at an angle of 70 degrees? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's about right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we please have photograph 253 from the same bundle. Look at the entry wound, which is almost from the top, and it is true that it -- the bullet did not arrive from the side but that the entry wound was made from a very high degree and exited at the heel almost vertically.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't draw the conclusion that this was the entry wound. I don't know if it's in the medical reports. I wasn't able to locate it in the medical reports. What I do know is that with the limbs especially in the areas where there's -- there are bones, it's very difficult to discern between the entry and exit wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the witness confirmed for us here explicitly that this was the entry wound and that the exit wound was at the heel below?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I believe this is also the witness that -- that testified that he was hit by a 50-calibre round, which -- which would have taken his foot off. So if the witness believes that was the entry and the exit wound, then according to him it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question concerning this: Is it in any way possible to have a wound inflicted at an angle of 70 degrees vertically to the body if Stotina is positioned to the right at some 40 to 50 metres high -- or rather, at an elevation of some 40 to 50 metres? Is that theoretically possible?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the conditions that you described it would be impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] There is another explanation of this, Your Honour, another sketch of mine which shows the possible trajectory of the bullet and the movement of the person, but unfortunately the time that I have left does not permit me to deal with it so we will move on. We can remain in open session because I will be dealing with technical matters only. Can we now have incident number 13 where a boy was hit? Can we have the first photograph placed, 3D 00843, photograph 202?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware of the fact that the place where this incidence took place was accurately marked?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is slightly different from the location that I marked on my sketch, but it's the approximate location, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see marked here two possible directions from which one could possibly shoot at the place where the boy stood?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that according to a witness's statement the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina sometimes held their forward positions here, if ever there was soldiers in here? But are you aware of this information?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were a soldier and were confronted with an army close by, would you come down the hill and open sniper fire? Would that not amount to an exaggerated exposure beyond any logic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be tactically [Realtime transcript read in error"technically"] very unwise to expose yourself in the open on the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. It's not "technically," but "tactically." Line ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, tactically. Could we now have photograph 3D 204. This photograph was taken from Stotina. Can you please flip it. Yes. Look at the large building over there, and then to the left of that high building you can see the building outside which this took place. I don't know if you recognise this. To the left of this largest building here is the building in front of which the incident took place. Therefore, from the positions at Stotina where you said the sniper shooter was located, is it possible to see the scene of the incident on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph it's impossible because the tan-coloured building was built after the incident, which now blocks the view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was another building that was built, and the roof of that building is facing quite a different direction. Could we have photograph 205, please. It will provide a clearer view. 205. Sir, do you recognise the building in front of which this took place by the balconies that we can see to the left here? Can we agree that this was indeed the building in front of which the boy was hit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building we see in the foreground with the brown roof, do you know that the building was there at the time of the incident? In other words, this is not the building that was built afterwards. Are you aware that this building was there at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator on scene pointed out to me that the brown building was built after the incident, so that's my information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you, but on the basis of the earlier photographs do you understand that the building that I was referring now and the other building were not one and the same building? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building on the right side, its roof is -- is going to the right, whereas the other building we saw on the other photograph had a roof that was turned differently. Are you aware of the fact that the building I was referring to earlier in that other photograph and this brigade here are not and the same?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you show me a picture of the other building, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go back to photograph 3D 202. Look at the roof here. There, 202. The roof-top we saw a moment ago is positioned perpendicular to this building, whereas the building marked B here is parallel -- or, rather, the ridge is parallel to the building. So my question is, are you aware of the fact this building marked B here and the building I showed awe moment ago are not one the same building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And you're not aware of the fact that the building we saw a moment ago at the other photograph existed get at the time of the incident? Are you aware of this or not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that my time is up, but I have only one incident left, not that I wouldn't want to go through all of them, but I don't have time. Could we have 3D 00850, please. We are still talking about number 13, in respect of which you established that the alleged position from which fire was opened was the -- was Mount Hum that was 300 metres away. At page 34 of the report it says that the possible position was Mountain Hum which was 800 metres, correction, away from the spot. Is this something you wrote?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something I wrote, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we please have the map enlarged. That's fine. A circle was drawn on this map, and the centre of that circle is the top of the Hum mount, and everything that is within that circle is up to 2.000 metres away from Mount Hum. Can you locate where approximately the house where the incident took place is? Can you tell roughly?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could have the map enlarged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can it be enlarged, please? Mount Hum. Do you see this parallel running through Mount Hum, and then across the Neretva there is a bridge, and then it says Luka up there. Do you see the word Luka?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These buildings are in fact located in an area called Luka to the left of the rectangle marked in black and then a bit up to the left. Do you see that now, near that road there? It's -- you should actually start from Mount Hum. Can you tell roughly where this would be?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house would be going from the -- the intersection --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show it to us? Can you indicate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I indicate on this map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the bridge across the Neretva River. We've seen it on many photographs. And then cross that bridge across the Neretva. There. Right.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the location of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Tell me, please, if the distance from the top of the Mount Hum to that red dot is 2.000 metres, how far is the top of Mount Hum to -- or, rather, if the previous distance to the circle was 2.000, how far would you say is Mount Hum to the dot you drew? Is it 1.400 to 1.500 metres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there has been a mistake, because one square on a geographical map is usually depicted -- this is 1:50.000 scale, which means that every square is 1 kilometres, and the diameter of the complete circle is 2 kilometres. So the distance from Mount Hum to the location would be 6 to 800 metres on this map. This location on the map is 1 kilometre, this distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I cannot bring any rulers here, but -- right. Right. There is an error. Correct. It's 1 kilometre. This is a mistake. So the diameter is 2 kilometres, and half of it is 1 kilometre, but let us leave it at that. What is the distance from the top of Hum hill to the point you marked, 800 -- right. It's written correctly. My apologies. My apologies. It's a mistake that I made. Just one last thing, please. Is it true that from the top of Hum hill, since there is first a mild slope, then a sharper slope, the position where the boy was hit is completely invisible. From Hum hill you cannot see the incident site and vice versa. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you for all these answers. I'm sorry that I have no more time to go through the other incidents so as to see if they make sense geometrically and otherwise, but two days was too short a time for you to arrive at absolutely accurate and precise data. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. 4D now. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just have one technical matter to raise in connection with what Mr. -- General Praljak said. This map is 1:50.000 in scale, and the distance is 4 centimetres on the map. So that should be 2 kilometres. It is a good map indeed, because in principle between two measurements, from 96 to 98, there are 2 kilometres. This distance is equal to the distance from Hum hill. I claim that there are 4 centimetres here and that makes 2 kilometres on this map. I just want my objection on record and then we can leave it to experts. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Yes. The fact remains it is 2 kilometres. So the distance from the top of Hum hill to the location of the house is 1.500 to 1.600 metres. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden, if you have precise information about an entry and exit wound and you also have precise information about where the victim was standing and at what angle at the point of impact, it's correct, is it, that you can within really quite a fine tolerance, you can state with precision the direction from which the shot must have come?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the precise position and placement of the body is known, then it is possible to get a reasonably accurate direction of fire, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You need those elements --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That I've described. You need entry and exit wound or at least entry wound precision, position and angle of body --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- and then you can get --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- with pretty good precision?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exact position of the body at the time of the entry wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And the other way round. If you start with a fixed, definite location or direction, let's say direction from which the shot has come, and you also have precise information about, let us say, the entry and the exit wound, you can also work out, with a high degree of precision, the angle at which the victim's body must have been standing at the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In the first situation, then, where we're working from the victim's body position and the wounds, but we're work being from the victim's body position, let's take as examples incidence 1 and incidence 10, and you've shown --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You've shown enormous familiarity with those incidents. Your know exactly the once I'm talking about. 1 near the bridge and 10 from the river, fetching water at the river. So they're both down by the river. And we can agree, can't we that a feature of each of those cases is that until we get to such questions as to the precise position of the victim's body there is actually a wide range of possibilities, isn't there, as far as location of the gunman is concerned?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually it's not that wide a range of possibilities. There are things in -- yeah, to be taken in consideration technically. While technically it would be possible for a wider range of possibilities, if I would have to -- if I would have to take a shot at a target and I would have to stand out -- completely out in the open, that -- technically it would be possible for me to stand in that position and shoot at the target and hit the target, but technically it would be very unwise. So it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I want to be quite precise. I'm not talking at the moment about preferred locations and where a professional sniper might locate himself and all the other factors which you bring into play here and there to explain why such-and-such a location is more probable. In each of those cases there is, in fact -- physically there is a quite wide arc, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So that it follows that -- it follows just mathematically or arithmetically, doesn't it, if the victim's body is turned through an angle of 15 degrees that alters the direction of the shot by the corresponding 15 degrees?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Working the other way round quite a lot of people working in this matter as informants did, if we start from a fixed idea of where the shot came from and you have the other elements of the information, you've got the entry and the exit wound, then - I think you confirmed this a few minutes ago - you can then work out the angle at which the victim's body must have been placed to suffer that wound from that specific location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And in a significant number of cases where there is a very clear entry and exit wound, or perhaps even a very clear entry wound, it doesn't actually require, with all respect to your expertise, Mr. van der Weijden, it doesn't require a degree of expertise to work that out, does it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the technical part, no. As long as we have knowledge of geometry it could be worked out, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's pretty straightforward?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: If I've been shot it doesn't matter particularly for the record where to make the point, if I've been shot here in my back and I know or if I have a got a fixed idea where I was shot from, it's not at all difficult for me to turn my body to the position in which I must have been to be shot there from that position; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is where I don't completely agree. There is some -- something called -- well, there are -- the memory of people is not always what the physical conditions exactly are at the time of some things happening. In the military there's the fog of war. As people -- they know they're hit but are not completely able to exactly be in the same position at exact time of when they're hit. So it's -- I -- I agree that on a lot of the case, a lot of the incidents the victims when they show their self, where they show where they're hit on the DVD, for me it doesn't necessarily mean -- if I've -- especially in the case of my -- of the hill, where the victim is hit in the hill, in case number 10, for an incident happening 10 years ago it would be very difficult for me to -- if only for one moment I have my heel turned to the right or to the left, it can alter the complete situation. So it's -- it's very -- yeah. For me the biggest difficulty was is the -- the memory of the victims, is it correct as to where the exact location or at the exact position their body was in at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, the complete list of incidents, it's numbers 1 to 14 but with two -- two numbers taken out, numbers 5 and 12. So we've got 12 incidents here and they're on different dates, the earliest being 13th of May, 1993, and the latest being the 2nd of March, 1994. Just one, possibly two dates -- I think there was just one date where there were two incidents on the same date. It's right, is it, that you have yourself no knowledge of what was happening -- apart from what you've been told about the specific incidents, you have no knowledge of what was happening on any of those dates in terms of what military combat there was, what attacks, what activity there was in the area? You had not been briefed on that and you do not know any of that, do you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Ibrisimovic, any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... questions, Mr. President. We have time to other Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does Prosecution have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I have just one question but I would like to simply put on the record the fact that during the cross-examination of General Praljak the fact that the Prosecution didn't object to a number of questions does -- should not in any way be taken to imply that in any way we agree with any of his characterisations of any of the evidence given to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Lieutenant van der Weijden, I just have one question, if you will. It follows from a number of questions put to you during the course of cross-examination, and the question is this, sir: What action should a shooter take in the event that he or she is unable to distinguish between the civilian or combatant status of the intended target?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the rules of engagement that I've been provided with in my operations, it has always been to withhold fire until positive identification of enemy personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much on behalf of myself and my colleagues for coming here to give testimony. Your testimony was in two steps, and unfortunately we were not able to do anything else. My best wishes for you to continue your mission.
